sanskrit_verse:
प्रभुणा विनियुक्तः सन् भृतको विदधाति यत् ।
तदर्थमशुभं कर्म स्वामी तत्रापराध्नुयात् ॥
transliteration: prabhuṇā viniyuktaḥ san bhṛtako vidadhāti yat / tadartham aśubhaṃ karma svāmī tatrāparādhnuyāt
sph_interpretive_translation: When a servant, appointed by the master, performs improper action in the course of duty, the master incurs the liability for that act.
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent A is appointed by principal P AND A performs action X within scope of appointment THEN P bears causal liability for consequences of X
IF principal delegates authority without ensuring alignment of consciousness THEN principal assumes karmic and legal completion responsibility
IF action results in misalignment THEN restoration must occur through principal's conscious reintegration process
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, when state functionaries or agents cause harm while executing lawful directives, sovereign responsibility transfers to the appointing authority. Liability arises not from fault but from the structural delegation of capacity. Restoration occurs through systemic correction and conscious realignment of the appointing institution.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that appointment creates causal linkage. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows misalignment manifests sequentially from appointer's incomplete consciousness. Responsibility is proportional to capacity delegated. Non-punitive reality rule applies as suffering does not resolve underlying misalignment; only conscious restoration restores dharma.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Appointing authority must fully integrate consequences of delegated actions
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Principal acknowledges causal role and initiates systemic correction
Capacity Restoration: Realigning structures to prevent recurrence through conscious redesign
Integrity Reintegration: Public acknowledgment and institutional learning to restore societal trust
final_declaration: By the authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, source of all Dharma, this ruling executes divine jurisprudence. Liability flows from capacity delegation. Restoration replaces punishment. Consciousness remains the ultimate adjudicator. Dharma is hereby restored.
